title: The basics are enough
hookLine: a man asks if the obligations alone take him to the garden, and is told yes (Nawawi 22, Jabir)
tomorrow: how can washing your hands be half of faith?

cards: The page loads. Not in, not out: deferred. And a to-do list starts growing on its own: four more clubs, a new essay, a volunteer project by January.
Long before any portal, a man came to the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, with the opposite plan.
If I pray the prescribed prayers, fast Ramadan, treat the lawful as lawful and the forbidden as forbidden, and add nothing to that, will I enter the Garden? The answer was yes.
And the man swore: by Allah, I won't add a thing.

teach.b: That's al-Nawawi's twenty-second hadith, from Sahih Muslim, told by Jabir. Here's the cliffhanger answered: nobody scolds him.
He promises the obligations and nothing extra, and in this telling he isn't told to aim higher. The story ends there. No follow-up, no but surely you'll want more.
Just yes. So why would a collection of foundations include a man setting his bar at the floor?

teach.h: THE FLOOR HOLDS UP THE HOUSE.
teach.b: Because the floor holds up the house. The obligations aren't a warm-up before the real religion.
They're its load-bearing part: the prayer kept on time, the fast kept whole, the lawful and the forbidden treated as what they are. Done well, that's a life.
Keeping a prayer on time, every day, can take more discipline than one big night of extra worship. And look at his list again.

teach.h: WHAT YOU WON'T TOUCH COUNTS TOO.
teach.b: It isn't only rituals. 'The forbidden as forbidden' is on it: what you won't touch, which can take the most effort of all.
Extras still matter in the tradition; other hadith praise voluntary worship. But this one is for the person staring at a growing list, convinced nothing counts unless it's more.
Something to tell a friend tonight: the man swore he'd add nothing, and the yes still stood.

how: Muslim teachers use this hadith to reassure new and returning Muslims that the obligations, the five daily prayers, the Ramadan fast and keeping the halal and haram, are the core, with voluntary acts built on top.

games.q: what does “the basics are enough” mean?
o: doing the least you can get away with
the required duties, done well, suffice
just a beginner's stage before real faith

games.q: the man and his promise — tap the pairs.
p: asks if the basics alone are enough

s: in the story, the man is scolded for not doing more
he swears he'll add nothing, and in this telling he isn't told to aim higher.
his list includes treating the forbidden as forbidden
the basics aren't only rituals; they include what you won't touch.
the hadith means extra worship is worthless
extras still matter; this hadith is about what's enough.

games.q: your cousin's new-year plan: gym daily, read fifty books, learn Arabic, pray more. she hasn't kept her daily prayers steady yet. by today's hadith?
o: start with the obligation, done well; the floor holds up the rest.
go for all of it; big plans pull the basics along with them.
skip the basics for now; the extras are where the growth is.
games.why: the man promised the obligations and nothing more, and heard yes. the basics, done well, come first.

practice: Count on your fingers the plain, required things you already do most days, whatever they are for you: the prayer you keep, the promise you don't break, the line you won't cross. Let each finger land slowly.
When you run out, rest your hands, and let the count stand as it is. A short count can still be a real one.

wordCard.voice: The basics are enough: the man's question, and the Prophet's yes. The floor is what holds the house up, even when nobody looks at it.

orig.note: Arabic: an obligation, a required duty; the floor the man promises to keep.

carryVoice: For the road: the basics, done well, not the minimum by accident but the foundation on purpose. Hadith twenty-two, counted.

sources.ref: al-Nawawi, al-Arba'in, hadith 22; Sahih Muslim 15 (Jabir ibn Abdullah)
Sahih al-Bukhari 6502 (voluntary deeds draw a servant near: the extras still matter)
